headline: THE RECONSTRUCTION IS NOT ONE BROKEN THING. 33 domain findings merge to 31 distinct defects under 14 root-cause codes, and 23 of the 31 are BLOCKER or MAJOR. Three structural facts organise all of them. (1) THE PIPELINE OBSERVES THROUGH CLOSED HAND-CURATED ALLOWLISTS AND EVERY PROPERTY OUTSIDE THEM IS SILENTLY REPLACED BY THE CSS INITIAL VALUE, WHICH IS ALMOST NEVER A SAFE DEFAULT: opacity initial 1 makes a suppressed box paint at full strength (91.6% of /pricing desktop's changed pixels), mask-composite initial `add` turns a 3-layer intersect fade opaque (74% of the home page's changed pixels over 23.8% of its area), fill initial black inverts every icon on a dark ground (13.64:1 -> 1.15:1 contrast), stroke initial none deletes artwork outright, and -webkit-font-smoothing initial `auto` is precisely the wrong value on macOS. 17 of 31 entries are an allowlist omission. (2) THE MEASURED FIDELITY NUMBER CANNOT SEE MOST OF THIS AND, WHERE IT CAN, IT RANKS IT BACKWARDS. src/reconstruction-qa/capture-page.ts:46 sets QA_STYLE_PROPERTIES = STYLE_WHITELIST, so the verifier's comparison vocabulary IS the loss channel and a property the Observer never captured is read on neither side; `pseudo` appears in ZERO files under src/reconstruction-qa/; the one purpose-built font escape hatch requires fontFamilyMismatchNodes > 0 while the clone's computed font-family STRING is byte-identical to the source's, so it is structurally unfireable in exactly the total-substitution case it exists for (shipped final-summary.json has NO font-family key in styleMismatchByProperty and requiresFontBindingObservation 0 across all 12 classifications, on a lineage where zero faces loaded on 8/8 routes); screenshot-diff.ts:29 states outright 'No PASS score. Nothing here returns a verdict'; and emit-diffs.ts:77/:235 wraps the ENTIRE geometry emission in `if (!unstable)`, so a per-load letter-scramble on one /security heading suppressed the corpus's cleanest layout finding (an exact 80.00px band displacement, measured in the page artifact and emitted as zero diffs). (3) THE TWO WORST DEFECTS IN THE CORPUS WERE NEVER PHOTOGRAPHED. At 1024-1231px /pricing hides 507 nodes and the comparison table loses its header row and three of four plan columns; at 391-914px all 8 routes render as a 390px column pinned to the left of the canvas. Neither width is in the observed profile set, so both contribute exactly 0.0000 to every published fidelity number. FIXING THE TOP TWO ENTRIES TOGETHER - materialize the real faces and capture text rasterization - removes 80.4% / 85.8% / 79.5% of changed pixels on /security, /integrations and /customers/automattic and takes /integrations to a >=16/255 changed ratio of 0.00048, i.e. effectively text-exact; they are multiplicative and neither is worth much alone. The flagship home page is the exception and stays at 0.1878 with perfect typography, its residual being SVG paint, mask compositing, film-grain texture and video frames. FINALLY, THE HEADLINE BAND 0.0235-0.4953 IS NOT A COMPARABLE NUMBER: it is a >=1/255-any-channel rule whose perceptible fraction ranges from 26% (r000001 desktop) to 98% (r000003 desktop), which is why this document ranks by geometry, semantics and region crops, and reports pixel share only as an attributed causal figure.

mismatches.earliestLossPoint: OBSERVATION - src/observer/collect-dom.ts:741-772. Three stacked defects in one 30-line block: (a) :745-748 `try { rules = sheet.cssRules } catch { continue; }` silently drops every cross-origin stylesheet with no counter, no flag and no artifact field, and 100% of this site's CSS is cross-origin; (b) the loop iterates only each sheet's TOP-LEVEL rules and never recurses into grouping rules, unlike the layout-rule visitor 480 lines earlier, so a face nested in @layer/@media is lost even from a readable sheet; (c) it records only {url, family} and no descriptors (weight range, style, unicode-range, display), so a variable axis could not be reconstructed even from a successful capture. The loss then re-occurs at three further points that each independently guarantee failure: src/observer/collect-assets.ts:228-231 drops the family; src/assets/fonts.ts:200-203 hardcodes status 'license-needs-review' and selfHostApproved:false for EVERY family unconditionally; and src/reconstruction/style-generator.ts contains the substring 'font' ZERO times in 228 lines and has no at-rule emission channel at all, so no @font-face could be written even from a perfect capture. Remediation is three changes, not one.
mismatches.smallestPlausibleGenericCorrection: Give font-face capture a channel that does not depend on same-origin CSSOM: read the browser's own loaded-font set, which enumerates every materialized face with its family, style, weight range and unicode range regardless of stylesheet origin, and resolve each face's source URL; keep the family binding on the resulting font asset instead of discarding it; and give the stylesheet generator an at-rule emission channel so a captured face can be written out. Make the cross-origin skip and the top-level-only iteration honest: count and report skipped sheets and recurse into grouping rules. Report 'family requested by N computed styles but no face recovered' as a named, counted artifact field so the absence is never silent.

driftAccounting.measuredDeltaAttributableToSourceVarianc: ZERO on 16 of the 19 audited pairs, by construction. Those 16 are scored against source.ACCEPTED.png, verified sha256-identical to the stored August observation screenshot, so post-observation source change cannot enter the number at all. On the 3 CURRENT_SOURCE-only 'wide' pairs (r000001, r000004, r000007) drift is fully mixed in and can be large: on the r000001 desktop analogue 55.4% of clone-vs-live changed pixels are pixels where the clone MATCHES August truth (0.2073 against August vs 0.4785 against live, a 2.31x inflation). Measured ACCEPTED-vs-CURRENT_SOURCE drift per route at the >=1/255 rule: r000001 0.4521, r000006 0.2857, r000003 0.0382, r000007 0.0343, r000008 0.0026, r000002 0.0003, r000004 0.0002, r000005 0.0001, against a same-session capture-nondeterminism floor of 0.03%-1.04%.
driftAccounting.attributableToBrokenReference: ONE PAIR, r000002 /changelog mobile. Its published 0.2221 is approximately 53% broken reference and 47% real clone delta: the ACCEPTED reference is a 73,446px column at 1.155% ink with only the sticky header, one bell icon, seven 35px video control strips and one poster painted, while the clone renders the full page at 11.04% ink and the observation's own DOM records 905 effectively-visible nodes. Scoring the clone against same-session PAINTED live viewport tiles gives 0.0779-0.1177 (mean 0.1031). Consequence for the rest of this document: every cluster scored on r000002/mobile - including the video-poster one - has a meaningless pixel share, so no entry here anchors on that pair.
driftAccounting.attributableToReconstruction: Everything else. Concretely: on the 16 drift-immune pairs the entire measured delta is the reconstruction's, and the clone side is itself drift-immune - bit-identical between wave-1's capture and independent re-captures a day later on 6/6 desktop routes (and 0 differing pixels on the two routes the pseudo verifier re-captured), despite the served clone making 20-66 live third-party fetches per page. Two further shares must be subtracted before calling the remainder a fidelity defect: animation/per-load randomisation variance (RC-31; ~14% of /plan desktop's changed pixels is one hero video frame) and the sub-perceptual fraction of the >=1/255 metric (RC-30; 74% of r000001 desktop's 'change' is below a 32/255 threshold).
driftAccounting.method: Every counterfactual quoted in this document was scored against the ACCEPTED August reference, with all variants in any one comparison captured in the same session against the same byte-identical PNG and with document height verified unchanged so no reflow confound exists. Live linear.app captures made on 2026-08-28/29 are labelled CURRENT_SOURCE throughout and are used ONLY to read which property the source declares - never as historical pixel truth. Where a live capture is the reference (the 3 wide pairs) the pair is named and its number is excluded from any fidelity conclusion.

The argument 'the clone scores within 0.1% against both references therefore the references agree' is WITHDRAWN as a non-sequitur. 41%-98% of drifted pixels land where the clone was already wrong and the remainder nearly cancels (r000003: 269,027 drifted pixels for a net score change of -16,703). The conclusion survives on the correct ground instead: 16 of 19 pairs are scored against ACCEPTED by construction.

'The /changelog mobile reference is a one-off corrupt file' is WITHDRAWN: the blank REPRODUCES on the live page today at 390x844 DSF3 and not at DSF1 (14.10% ink) or DSF2 (12.24%), placing the failure at the renderer's >65,535 device-px full-page bitmap limit rather than in the stored file. newlyDiscovered.what: -webkit-font-smoothing is never observed, and it is CO-EQUAL with the missing @font-face rather than a residual.
newlyDiscovered.whyNew: No wave-1 cluster family named it and both C1-FONT skeptics tested only @font-face, so they measured the smaller half of the typography defect. It is invisible until the face is right (5.0%/4.3%/2.1%/0.9% alone) and then removes the majority of what the font fix leaves behind (cumulative 80.4%/85.8%/79.5%). It is also the mechanism behind every wave-1 cluster that recorded '+25-42% more ink at IDENTICAL advance width' - a signature typeface substitution cannot produce, because substitution also moves advances.

newlyDiscovered.what: At 1024-1231.98px the /pricing comparison table loses its header row and three of four plan columns (507 emitted responsive-hidden rules on that page alone; 528 nodes hidden at 1024 vs 21 at 1440) with document height pinned at 6,348px, so the holes are dead space.
newlyDiscovered.whyNew: No source/clone pair exists at any width in that band - the observed profiles are 390 and 1440 and the audit's third profile is 1920 - so wave 1 could not have seen it. The observer's own layout probe measured the cliff (778 visible elements at 1024 vs 1268 at 1440) and nothing acted on it.

newlyDiscovered.what: At every width from 391px to 914px all 8 routes render as a 390px column pinned to the left of the canvas, with the rest of the viewport dead background.
newlyDiscovered.whyNew: Same reason - no observed or audited viewport lies in that range. Cause is a pure generator scoping defect: src/reconstruction/layout-inference.ts:136 and :470 hardcode the desktop subtree, so of the mobile-subtree selectors in the shipped sheet, 1,082 are ::before, 47 ::after, 4 interaction-reveal and ZERO are layout recovery.

newlyDiscovered.what: Both viewport subtrees ship in one document with SVG resource ids unscoped, so 161 of 161 mobile url(#) paint references on ALL 8 routes bind into the display:none desktop subtree and paint nothing.
newlyDiscovered.whyNew: Wave 1 saw the /plan symptom and marked the cluster recurringAcrossRoutes:false. The mechanism is 100% universal, and it is worth ~61% of /plan mobile's changed pixels. An 8-cell isolation matrix proves the conjunction is required (duplicate id alone paints; display:none alone paints) and three structurally different repairs give byte-identical screenshots.

newlyDiscovered.what: An entire /security content band sits exactly 80.00px too high because the generator re-emits a used height on a block whose last child collapsed its bottom margin through.
newlyDiscovered.whyNew: The QA measured it in the page artifact (y max 80.02/80.00 over 33/32 mismatched nodes) and emitted zero diff records, because the page was flagged environment-unstable by a per-load letter-scramble on one heading. Two verifiers independently reproduce the exact +80.00px restoration from a single height:auto.

newlyDiscovered.what: src/reconstruction/layout-inference.ts is a NET REGRESSION at its own truth viewport, contradicting its docstring guarantee at :19-22 that 'the 1440px rendering cannot regress by construction'.
newlyDiscovered.whyNew: Wave 1 flagged the /changelog symptom; wave 2 traced it to three specific arithmetic faults (containing block assumed to be the parent content box at :209-210; the display gate at :192 tests only the node's own display; the emitted ratio is a MEAN across probe widths so it misses even a correct containing block by 0.9px) and measured the tier at 409 nodes made worse against 1 made better, improving 5 of 8 desktop routes when removed and worsening none. Its only guard, TRUTH_SANITY_TOLERANCE_PX, compares two probe numbers and never lays a rule out.

newlyDiscovered.what: The /changelog mobile ACCEPTED reference screenshot is itself blank, and the blank is REPRODUCIBLE at 390x844 DSF3 above the renderer's 65,535 device-px full-page limit.
newlyDiscovered.whyNew: Wave 1 recorded the anomaly but attributed it to a corrupt file and defended it with a byte-size argument that does not hold. The correct diagnosis makes it a systematic observer defect that will recur on any tall mobile page, not a one-off.

newlyDiscovered.what: The visible counter defect lives on the PSEUDO-element, not the element: element-level counter-increment is 'none' on 100% of hosts, so adding counter properties to the element whitelist would fix nothing.
newlyDiscovered.whyNew: Corrects wave-1's attribution (which named STYLE_WHITELIST) in a way that changes which fix is correct. Also rescopes the damage ~11x: of 892 emitted content:counter(...) rules only the 80 decimal-leading-zero ones render visibly wrong; the 812 counter(prose-ul, disc) rules paint a disc regardless of counter value.

newlyDiscovered.what: The observation writes internally self-contradicting records - background-image:'none' alongside background-size:'256px 256px' and mix-blend-mode:'overlay' on 33 style tokens - and no stage notices.
newlyDiscovered.whyNew: Nobody had named the fingerprint. It is a cheap generic self-consistency check (an image-only modifier surviving on a layer whose image resolved to none is evidence the layer failed to resolve) that converts a silent flat-surface defect into a countable one.

newlyDiscovered.what: Font shaping (feature settings, variant-numeric, optical sizing, text-rendering) is captured nowhere and becomes the LARGEST remaining text defect the moment RC-01 lands - a further 47% of the surviving residual on /customers/automattic.
newlyDiscovered.whyNew: Structurally invisible while fonts are missing, so it could not have been found without the counterfactual ladder.

newlyDiscovered.what: The QA correction loop wrote its only correction into iterations/q001, never promoted it, and filed a final-summary under the uncorrected lineage declaring the defect resolved.
newlyDiscovered.whyNew: A release-provenance defect rather than a rendering one, found only by diffing the shipped globals.css against the q001 copy. Its pixel cost on this corpus is exactly 0 of 433,508,510 pixels, which is precisely why it survived.

newlyDiscovered.what: The single transferable rule the pipeline is missing: AN ALLOWLIST MAY DROP A PROPERTY ONLY WHEN THAT PROPERTY'S CSS INITIAL VALUE IS A SAFE DEFAULT.
newlyDiscovered.whyNew: Wave 1 catalogued the omissions individually. Stating the invariant explains why four independent omissions all fail loudly rather than degrading (opacity 1, mask-composite add, fill black, stroke none, font-smoothing auto are each the maximally wrong answer) and gives a mechanical test for every future whitelist entry.

claimsCorrectedByVerification.corrected: Re-wrapping affects 22.3% of multi-line runs. The ink figures are not reproducible as ink; they ARE reproducible as the smoothing effect, which is why they looked bimodal by weight.

claimsCorrectedByVerification.claim: C4-GEOMETRY: 'geometry parity is an artifact of baked pixel values, therefore the reconstruction only looks right'.
claimsCorrectedByVerification.corrected: Stripping all 5,740 baked width:<px> declarations changes document height by 0.00% on every desktop route; stripping all 5,779 baked height:<px> leaves 6/16 pairs within 2px and 9/16 within 0.3%; a full unfreeze of all baked pixel declarations still leaves a median 0.43% delta. Height parity is earned by faithfully reproduced box-model flow. Worse for the original story, un-baking makes PAINT worse on 4/4 routes tested (up to 13.3x on /integrations, 0.0235 -> 0.3131), because the observer records not one source CSS rule - the counterfactual to baking is collapse, not graceful reflow. The honest surviving defect is narrower and sharper: baking a USED value re-encodes it as an AUTHORED value and silently changes box-model semantics. Exactly three entries survive on that basis (RC-17, RC-18 and the conjunction RC-15). I re-counted the width figure myself at exactly 5,740; the height figure re-counts to 5,779, not 5,791.

claimsCorrectedByVerification.claim: C7-DRIFT: 'source drift explains almost none of the delta' supported by '/pricing and /customers drift is 0.0000 and 0.0007'.
claimsCorrectedByVerification.verdict: REFUTED (2 of 2 lenses) - the SUPPORT is wrong; the CONCLUSION is right for a different reason.
claimsCorrectedByVerification.corrected: Measured drift is 0.0343 and 0.0382, and wave 1's own handoff lists both routes under CONFIRMED DRIFT. The conclusion survives on the correct ground: 16 of 19 audited pairs are scored against a sha256-verified ACCEPTED reference, so drift cannot enter them at all. See driftAccounting.

claimsCorrectedByVerification.claim: C8-QAGATE: 'the QA schema cannot represent a paint difference at all'.
claimsCorrectedByVerification.verdict: REFUTED (2 of 2 lenses) as an absolute.
claimsCorrectedByVerification.corrected: The QA does compute a full-page pixel metric (screenshotChangedRatioMedian 0.1679 in the shipped summary) and does emit paint-adjacent classifications (canvas-background-mismatch 16, asset-hotlink-blocked 2). The precise and defensible statement is narrower and worse: the metric exists, is never turned into a classification or a gate, and the property-level channel that WOULD localise a paint difference is QA_STYLE_PROPERTIES = STYLE_WHITELIST, i.e. the loss channel itself - with no pseudo-element channel of any kind. See qaBlindSpots.

claimsCorrectedByVerification.verdict: PARTIALLY REFUTED (1 of 2 lenses); claim stands overall.

Wave-1's recurringAcrossRoutes:false is wrong at the mechanism level - 161 of 161 mobile url(#) references bind into the hidden desktop subtree on ALL 8 routes. The verifier's recompute (79.25% of the pair's error inside the overlays, 39.73% of page height) shows the claim UNDERSTATED rather than overstated.

claimsCorrectedByVerification.claim: Wave 1: '892 pseudo-elements hold a broken content:counter(...)'.
claimsCorrectedByVerification.verdict: Corrected by the typography domain, confirmed by me.
claimsCorrectedByVerification.corrected: 812 of the 892 use counter(prose-ul, disc), which paints a disc marker regardless of counter value and is visually unaffected. Only the 80 counter(line, decimal-leading-zero) rules render the visible '00'. Wave 1 overstated the visible damage roughly elevenfold. Wave-1's loss-point attribution (STYLE_WHITELIST) is also wrong: the increment lives on the pseudo, so the fix must target PSEUDO_STYLE_WHITELIST or the resolved-content channel.

claimsCorrectedByVerification.claim: Wave 1 (C-PAINT-01 area): '88.9% of /customers desktop's changed pixels'.
claimsCorrectedByVerification.corrected: 88.9% is a CONTAINMENT figure (changed pixels lying inside a rect). The causal number, from an opacity-suppression counterfactual, is 86.3%.

claimsCorrectedByVerification.claim: Wave 1 / layout: 'removing the recovered-layout tier drops /changelog desktop from 0.1491 to 0.0654'.
claimsCorrectedByVerification.verdict: UNRESOLVED - the two C5 lenses disagree and I decline to average them.
claimsCorrectedByVerification.corrected: The MECHANISM lens reports 0.1491 -> 0.0654 (56% reduction) and reproduces wave-1's published baseline exactly. The MEASUREMENT lens, on its own max-channel comparator, reports 0.1757 -> 0.1612 (8.3%) and flags the baseline discrepancy itself. Two problems block reconciliation: the lenses disagree on the BASELINE, so their reductions are not comparable; and the mechanism artifact is internally inconsistent - its NO_AUTO variant reports the improved ratio while its own measured widths for that variant are still the broken 303.27px/67.80px, the signature of state leaking across variants in one page session. The GEOMETRY is not in dispute (624 -> 303.27 restored to exactly 624.00; total width error 110,097px -> 1,200px; 409 nodes worse vs 1 better; 5 of 8 routes improved, 0 worsened) and RC-05 is ranked on that. Nothing in the ranking or the remediation depends on the disputed pixel figure.

whatThisDocumentDoesNotCover: Interactive after-states. Under the product definition of fidelity, hover, focus, scroll-driven sticky/fixed behaviour, menu-open and every other post-interaction state is in scope, and NONE of it was exercised on any pair in wave 1 or wave 2. All 31 entries are static full-page findings. The absence of interaction findings is an absence of measurement, not evidence of correctness.

Any route or viewport outside the 8 routes x {390, 1440} observed profiles plus the 1920 wide audit - except where an entry is specifically about an unobserved band (RC-08, RC-09, RC-18), which were measured on the served clone alone with no source reference available.

The template compilation stage and the authored customer site (data/linear.app/release-projects/wr28-switchyard). Every finding here is against the RAW reconstruction; wave-1's stage5 pixel diff is the only template evidence in the tree and no entry rests on it.

Any proposed fix. Every smallestPlausibleGenericCorrection is a description of the smallest generic change that would close the loss point, written so it can be planned - not a patch, not a design, and not validated by implementation.
